Subject: Next steps: dedicated sizing + technical deep-dive (60–75m) — availability

Hi Samir / Priyanka —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — great context on your fraud-detection pipeline and the bursty inference patterns during month-end reconciliation. Per our conversation, the two immediate next steps we recommended are:

1) A dedicated capacity sizing session (throughput & latency) so we can map your QPS / tail-latency SLOs to a proposed Redwood Dedicated pool.
2) A technical deep-dive / demo focused on the integration points (prefix cache, batching, and tokenization handling).

We usually combine these into a single 60–75 minute session (first 30–40 min sizing + the remainder for architecture + demo). Proposed slots (PDT):
- Tue Apr 20, 10:00–11:15 AM
- Wed Apr 21, 2:00–3:15 PM
- Thu Apr 22, 9:00–10:15 AM

Could you confirm which of the above works, or share two alternatives? If helpful, we can split into a 45-min sizing and separate 45-min demo — happy to accommodate.

Prep items (we’ll bring a draft capacity plan):
- A short CSV with representative load profile (requests/sec over 24–72h) and typical sequences (avg and 95th token lengths) — if you can attach, we’ll pre-populate sizing options.
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and expected concurrency per endpoint.
- Any model preferences (open model name / quantized variants) or constraints (e.g., private VPC).

I’ve looped in Priyom (SE) for the deep-dive and Marissa for commercial alignment.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive

Samir / Jordan — thanks for confirming — looking forward to Wed. Quick prep checklist from the SE side so our sizing is accurate:

1) Load profile: per-minute QPS for a 24–72h window (you already sent the CSV, thanks).
2) Example request payload(s): anonymized JSON of 2–3 typical scoring requests (we care about sequence length distribution).
3) Concurrency model: are bursts single-threaded clients (many rapid requests) or multiple simultaneous clients? If you can indicate concurrency by endpoint that helps.
4) Tokenization sample: average tokens / p95 / max tokens.
5) Model variant: which model you plan to run (or if you want our recommendations for a comparable open model + quantization).
6) Any network constraints (VPC, egress limits) or strict retention/compliance requirements.

During the call I’ll walk through: how we convert load profile -> batching strategy, KV cache sizing, and the preliminary GPU footprint for a Dedicated pool (including an option for burst capacity). If you can drop the sample payload and token counts into this Doc before the call it’ll speed things up: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Gf4-finovate-prep-checklist

See you Wed Apr 21, 2:00 PM PDT.

—
